title: Normalized Kummer computation of the simultaneous diagonal boundary
statement: Let ell be prime and invertible on an arbitrary scheme Y, put W=P1_Y times_Y P1_Y, and let D be a simultaneous derived reduction of scalar extension as in [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface]. Suppose a is the invertible canonical derived single counit at the supported integral constant. Then there exist a strict Z_ell-module system H, an identification of its underlying abelian tower with the actual roots-of-unity tower, and an isomorphism b from D applied to shifted comparison units to H[2]. At each positive exponent n+1 the source and target identifications preserve respectively the quotient generator and the specified roots-to-Tate-line map. Under these identifications, the degree-two Ext class corresponding to a inverse followed by D of the positive integral boundary followed by b equals the complete finite Cartier class restricted from the residue coefficients to Z_ell.

source.place: Proof steps 5--7: normalized finite source, strict Kummer target, and equality of the full finite Cartier boundary

proof.text: Pull invertibility of ell to the surface. At each level the ordinary source quotient theorem supplies an isomorphism satisfying DiagonalSourceNormalization. Unfold that predicate to obtain its generator equation while retaining the original normalization.

Apply strict Kummer target transport to obtain one strict system, its roots identification and derived comparison, and normalized finite target isomorphisms. Its arbitrary-arrow formula applies to the integral diagonal boundary. The named negativeExtProduct is exactly the negative Yoneda product, without any change of sign convention.

Apply the proved finite Cartier normalization. It first uses sign cancellation and full scalar-adjunct Cartier uniqueness to identify the residue-linear class, then applies coefficient restriction to this equality. Its conclusion is exactly the finite-class predicate of the diagonal interface.

Specialize the proved sheaf Kummer assembly to the diagonal surface, the supported integral source and the pole boundary. Supply the normalized ordinary quotient, its generator equation, and the proved finite Cartier normalization implication. The scheme assembly supplies the single strict target and substitutes its evaluated-arrow equation into the exact original finite-class predicate, preserving both normalizations.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_kummer_reduction (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (hY : IsUnit (ℓ : Γ(Y, ⊤)))
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ (diagonalSurface Y))]
    (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (diagonalScalarExtension ℓ (diagonalSurface Y)))
    (a : D.T.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (diagonalIntegralSource Y)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (D.ordinary.E.obj (diagonalIntegralSource Y)))
    (ha : a.hom = diagonalDerivedSingleCounit ℓ
      (diagonalScalarExtension ℓ (diagonalSurface Y)) D (diagonalIntegralSource Y)) :
    diagonalBoundaryTarget ℓ Y hY D a
